subject: Shoulder Capacity & Autoscale Handshake — Orchid Health Dedicated Deal
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@orchidhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing question for peak-care window (Orchid / Redwood)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we scope the Dedicated commitment for Orchid, a couple of ops questions came up on our side around shoulder capacity and how Redwood's autoscale behaves during our weekly peak-care windows (Mon/Wed 11:00-14:00 PT):

- We need a predictable headroom policy for short bursts (30–90s spikes) that doesn't consume our reserved slab permanently.
- We also want a clear eviction/backoff behavior if the reserved pool saturates and the ephemeral shoulder pool is exhausted.

Can you share a proposed guardrail (SLA/ops) and an example monthly charge impact if we use ephemeral shoulder capacity 10% of committed baseline for up to 45 minutes/week? I've attached our model profile and the usage sketch.

Appreciate it — Sara

Attachments: orchid_madcap_model_profile.pdf (pdf)

--
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Operations | Orchid Health
Sara.Lim@orchidhealth.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question for peak-care window (Orchid / Redwood)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the model profile. Looping in Karthik and Ben to propose an operational handshake and cost example.

High level from my side: we normally recommend a two-tier approach for Dedicated customers with predictable weekly spikes:

1) Shoulder (ephemeral) pool: short-lived preemptible GPUs that can be allocated on top of the reserved slab for burst windows. Charged at a premium delta (approx +45–65% per token-hour vs reserved), and reclaimed first on contention.
2) Autoscale policy: soft-limit ramp where requests hit the ephemeral pool up to a configured headroom percent; beyond that we backpressure and route to a cheaper compatible model variant.

We will produce a sample slab matrix and a monthly impact estimate for your 10% shoulder usage for 45 minutes/week.

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Irene.Choi@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing question for peak-care window (Orchid / Redwood)

Irene / team — sketched a concrete proposal below (numbers rough, will calibrate once Orchid's token/sec profile is passed through our estimator):

Proposal:
- Baseline reserved slab: 120 A100-equivalent GPU-hours (committed).
- Shoulder (ephemeral) buffer: 12 GPU-hours (10% of baseline) available in a short-lived pool. Policy: ephemeral instances are preemptible after 60s idle and evicted in reverse-allocation order.
- Autoscale behavior: continuous batching enabled; headroom percent = 10% baseline; burst window policy = 45 min/week with sliding-window enforcement; if ephemeral exhausted, fallback routing to quantized model variant (latency SLO relaxed from 120ms -> 200ms).
- Billing: ephemeral usage billed hourly with a multiplier (1.55x) on per-GPU token-hour; monthly example: 12 GPU-hours * 4 weeks * 1.55x = 74.4 billable GPU-hours delta.

Operational guardrails to include in the amendment:
- Preemption notice: 10s SOA best-effort signal before eviction (for graceful checkpointing).
- Throttle priority: live inference > batch backfill.
- Incident escalation: Redwood oncall if ephemeral pool unresponsive for >2 min during peak window.

Attachments: proposed-slab-matrix.csv (csv)

Thoughts: Ben — does this align with our typical shoulder SLA language? Monica — any concerns on on-call exposure for a health-care customer?

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Services
Karthik.Iyer@redwood.com
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@orchidhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question for peak-care window (Orchid / Redwood)

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A couple follow-ups from our SRE and procurement: 

- Can you confirm the expected latency delta to the quantized fallback for our 512-token median request? Is the 200ms SLO a worst-case or median?
- For billing: will the ephemeral multiplier apply to reserved bursts only or to any ephemeral instance (including cross-account opportunistic allocation)? We need the amendment language to avoid unexpected cross-account billing.

Also, Ben mentioned integrating a short audit log export for evictions — could Redwood provide an S3 export of eviction events and preemption notices for our SOC review? That would let us map user-impacted requests back to audit traces.

We'd like to get a draft amendment in the next week to stabilize procurement.

Best,
Sara

--
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Operations | Orchid Health
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question for peak-care window (Orchid / Redwood)

Sara — thanks, all good asks. Consolidated answers and next steps below.

1) Latency delta: the 200ms is a 95th-percentile SLO for the quantized fallback at 512 tokens under the proposed slab sizing. Median should remain ~120–140ms in our experiments. We'll include perf percentiles in the amendment exhibit.

2) Billing boundary: ephemeral multiplier applies only to shoulder instances allocated against your Dedicated contract. We will not bill cross-account opportunistic allocations to Orchid. We'll add explicit language in the amendment that ephemeral instances for your slab are namespace-scoped and billed only to ORC-3472.

3) Eviction audit export: yes — we can provision a daily S3 export (CSV) of eviction/preemption events and attach request IDs. We'll include a sample schema in the amendment.

Next steps:
- Karthik to bake perf percentiles and a revised slab CSV (will move the proposed-slab-matrix.csv -> final) by 6/30.
- Legal/procurement: I'll push the draft amendment (orchid-autoscale-sla-draft.docx) to DocuSign and share the link once Ben signs off on SLA language.

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/drive/ORC-3472-autoscale-amendment
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ORC-3472

I'll follow up with Ben and Monica offline and get the amendment ready for your review.

Thanks — Irene
